notes:
Summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS evaluating move from Hosted API trial -> Dedicated for production scoring and chat assistant. Heavy emphasis on predictable latency and cost. Trial results below.

Trial metrics (hosted API trial): avg QPS: 4.2 across business hours; peak sustained QPS: 18 for 10m windows; typical concurrency (streaming chat sessions): 6–8 active users, peak 22.
Token mix (observed): prompt tokens ~ 75%, completion tokens ~25% per request; median request ~ 850 tokens, 95th pct ~ 3,200 tokens.
Latency targets: p95 generation < 650ms (desired), current hosted p95 ~ 420ms for small context flows; larger multi-doc summarization p95 ~ 1.1s.
Throughput needs for Dedicated sizing: baseline target 30 QPS sustained with burst to 90 QPS for 15m windows; concurrency budget for KV/cache-friendly chat: target 50 concurrent sessions.
Cost sensitivity: internal goal reduce per-token cost by 35% vs hosted list pricing via batching/quantization and Dedicated discounts.
Model preferences: prefer open/Redwood-verified model family; will consider quantized 4-bit variants for cost. Fallback policy: routed to cheaper variant for non-critical requests.
Security: require SSO/SAML, audit logging, KMS integration; legal insisting on data residency in NA for PII fields.
POC asks: capacity-sizing workshop to map QPS->GPUpool config, recommended concurrency per server, estimated token-hours, pricing tiers for reserved vs burst capacity.
Quote: "We liked the latency numbers on hosted but need pricing certainty and a predictable cost model before committing to Dedicated."

Recent links: see pricing deck + security FAQ in Drive. Short term next: run Dedicated-capacity POC with 2-week ramp and autoscale rules; deliver estimate and draft SOW by 2026-03-05.
